headline: FinCEN cuts crypto exchange MEXC Global off from the US financial system over $16bn in illicit flows

sources: US Treasury (OFAC designations press release sb0686 + FinCEN Section 9714 order sb0685, Nov 6, 2026; @USTreasury X post); Al Jazeera (2026-11-07T04:50:46Z); Times of India; Economic Times (Reuters wire); CoinDesk; Tradin
fault_line: Sanctions enforcement or crypto crackdown? Cutting a top-20 exchange off dollar rails chokes Iran's money pipeline -- or proves Washington will police the whole crypto industry.

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- US Treasury, primary source] On Nov 6, 2026, OFAC designated eight Canada-based money services businesses under Executive Order 13902 for facilitating transactions with sanctioned Iranian entities: Diverse Trade Inc (Million Exchange), 1380079 BC Ltd (Amin Exchange), Top PC Technician Inc, NIA Nations Currency Ltd, 2397639 Ontario Ltd (Farah Exchange), CCC Inc, B Galaxy Inc (Cryptoyal), Darvish Exchange (Ontario + British Columbia). Action coordinated with FinCEN and Canada's FINTRAC + DEA, under Operation Economic Outcast (launched August 2026). [VERIFIED FACT -- FinCEN order] Separately the same day, FinCEN issued an order under Section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act effectively cutting Seychelles-incorporated crypto exchange MEXC Global off from the US financial system (US institutions barred from processing its transfers). FinCEN alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16bn in illicit transactions May 2021-May 2026: ~$1.5bn linked to Russian sanctions evasion incl. sanctioned exchanges Garantex and successor Grinex (as recently as June 2026); ~$1bn in direct transfers to 40+ Iranian crypto exchanges; $22m linked to the Central Bank of Iran and the IRGC/Quds Force; total Iran exposure ~$1.87bn (11.2% of the total). MEXC processed >$1bn/day as of June 2026 and held ~$4.48bn in assets (DefiLlama). MEXC is the LARGEST exchange ever hit under Section 9714. The order takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication (not yet published at last check). [CONTEXT] Pattern: Nobitex (Iran's largest crypto exchange) sanctioned June 2026; BitBank sanctioned September 2026 over alleged bitcoin transfers to the IRGC. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent: Canada 'cannot be a safe haven for illicit financial facilitators'.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct publisher families with declared tiers: US Treasury (T1, STATE US, primary source), Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA), Times Group (T3 -- Times of India + Economic Times are one family). CoinDesk, Firstpost, Blockonomi, TradingView relays and Gulf News have NO declared tier in the registry -- reported with attribution only, they do not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: MEXC says it is operating normally, has launched a review of its AML/sanctions controls and an independent review; no criminal charges announced against the eight firms and no asset seizures beyond standard OFAC blocking language. The FinCEN order formally rests on Section 9714, a Russia-focused AML provision -- the Iran/North Korea strands ride on the Russian finding, so the order's legal hook is Russian illicit finance, not Iranian. The $16bn figure is an allegation ('at least $16 billion in alleged illicit transactions'), not a proven total; The Edge's calculation puts the figure at $16.7bn. The transfer ban is not yet in force (30 days after Federal Register publication).
sections.why_matters: The $16 billion pipeline: how Iran moved money through crypto -- and the day the US cut its biggest pipe.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Treasury announcement Fri Nov 6 US; AJ published 2026-11-07T04:50:46Z = 08:50 ; zero 'MEXC'/'Economic Outcast' mentions in any Nov 6 or Nov 7 scan) -- US Treasury OFAC designates 8 Canada-based money services firms for Iran sanctions evasion; FinCEN cuts crypto exchange MEXC Global off from the US financial system over $16bn in illicit flows
